title: Florida House, District 80
what_it_does: Represents District 80 (Parts of Collier, Lee) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Adam Botana
candidates.occupation: Small business owner (marine business, Bonita Springs); state representative since 2020
candidates.background: Adam Botana was born in Naples and lives in Bonita Springs, where he runs a small business on the water. He was first elected to the Florida House in 2020 and has represented District 80 (Bonita Springs, Estero, Fort Myers Beach and Sanibel) since 2022. He has volunteered with Habitat for Humanity.

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F (June 2, 2026) and HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026); local coverage noted the whole Lee delegation voted for HJR 203.

sources.title: Florida House floor vote, CS/HJR 1-F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), third reading

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (Feb. 13, 2025), which created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, funded state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and added criminal penalties tied to immigration status.

sources.title: Florida House floor vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), 2025 Special Session C, third reading

abortion.summary: Voted yes on SB 300 (2023), which limited most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy, on April 13, 2023.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, SB 300 (Heartbeat Protection Act, six-week abortion limit) passage (Yeas 70, Nays 40)

guns.summary: Voted yes on HB 543 (2023), which allowed carrying a concealed firearm without a state permit, on March 24, 2023.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/HB 543 (permitless concealed carry) passage, third reading (Yeas 76, Nays 32)

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which made every K-12 student eligible for a state scholarship usable at private schools or for home education, on March 17, 2023.

candidates.name: William Moskal
candidates.background: Bill Moskal has lived in Estero since 2012 and spent more than 40 years working in hospitals, health systems and community institutions, including Henry Ford Health, Tampa General Hospital, Cedars-Sinai, Baptist Health Miami and the Indian Health Service. He also served in the Peace Corps in Ukraine. He describes himself as a teacher, health care executive and consultant.

growth.summary: His campaign says infrastructure such as roads, schools, water systems and storm protection should come before development, and that residents rather than developers should set priorities.
growth.quote: Roads, schools, water systems, and storm protection should lead development, not chase it.
